headline: Juventus after the 0-3: Spalletti's side still clear favourites
summary: Juventus lost 0-3 at home to Lazio on Sunday, and Luciano Spalletti did not hide it: he said his side were inferior and lacked tempo, ideas and desire. Italian media report the club is standing by him, so the answer has to come from the players at Lecce. Lecce arrive from a 3-0 win at Udinese with 3.47 expected goals, but Di Francesco is patching up a midfield, with Coulibaly hurt and a second midfielder stopped. Across 10 bookmakers, margin removed, Juventus are 66.1% favourites, a little over a goal the better side on the handicap, with about 2.6 goals expected — a bad day, not a collapse.
read: Juventus travel to Lecce after a 0-3 home defeat to Lazio, with Spalletti publicly questioning his team's tempo and desire, yet the market still makes them 66.1% favourites — more than five times Lecce's chance. Lecce come in off a 3-0 win at Udinese but are patching up their midfield, and the market expects a little over 2.5 goals.

facts.fact: Juventus lost 0-3 at home to Lazio on Sunday.
facts.meaning: It is the only defeat in their last five and the most goals they have conceded in that run — the mood around the team is the story of this game.

facts.fact: Juventus are 66.1% favourites to win at Lecce.
facts.meaning: More likely than not, and by a wide margin — more than five times Lecce's 11.8% chance of a home win.

facts.fact: Spalletti said after the Lazio defeat that Juventus were inferior and that he did not like the lack of tempo, ideas, running and desire to work hard.
facts.meaning: The coach himself is questioning the team's attitude, so the response at Lecce is the sub-plot of the afternoon.

facts.fact: Lecce midfielder Coulibaly was forced off in the first half against Udinese, with his scan results and recovery time reported by Gazzetta.
facts.meaning: Lecce may face Juventus without one of their regular midfielders, right where Juventus are strongest.

facts.fact: Tuttosport report that Lecce coach Di Francesco is in an emergency for the Juventus match after another midfielder was forced to stop, forcing him to reshape the midfield.
facts.meaning: Two midfield absences would mean a patched-up engine room against the strongest part of Juventus' side.

facts.fact: Lecce won 3-0 at Udinese on Sunday and created 3.47 xG — the most they have managed in their last five matches.
facts.meaning: Di Francesco's side arrive on a high and are genuinely dangerous going forward, even with the midfield short.

facts.fact: The Asian handicap fair line is 1.19 in Juventus' favour — the market rates them a little over a goal better than Lecce.
facts.meaning: A one-goal Juventus win is roughly the break-even point, so Lecce's +1.25 start is close to a coin flip.

facts.fact: The market expects about 2.6 goals, with Over 2.5 at 52.5%.
facts.meaning: Three or more goals is more likely than not, but only just — this is not priced as a shoot-out.

sources.fact: Lecce midfielder Coulibaly was forced off in the first half against Udinese and his scan results and recovery time have been reported by Gazzetta.
Tuttosport report that Lecce coach Di Francesco is in an emergency for the Juventus match after another midfielder was forced to stop, forcing him to reshape the midfield.
Lecce won 3-0 away at Udinese on Sunday, with goals from Kiolonda Gaspar and Konan N'Dri.
Gazzetta report that no team in Serie A has scored as many goals from corners as Lecce this season, with Di Francesco's side relentless from set pieces.
Juventus lost 3-0 at home to Lazio on October 18 in Serie A.
Spalletti said after the Lazio defeat that Juventus were inferior and that he did not like the lack of tempo, ideas, running and desire to work hard.
Most Juventus fans left the Allianz Stadium in the closing minutes of the 3-0 home defeat to Lazio.
Buffon said the coach isn't the problem for Juventus and that Spalletti deserves time to turn things around.
